start: ^Mrs Kowalski: You're the one from IT?
^Mrs Kowalski: You all look like you've been up all night with this.
^Mrs Kowalski: The nurses are doing their best. Don't blame them if things slip.

c-0: ^Mrs Kowalski: Sore. I had my hip done on Monday, and they'd no beds on ortho, so here I am with the heart patients.
^Mrs Kowalski: My daughter's coming at visiting. She'll have questions for all of you, believe me.
c-1: ^Mrs Kowalski: It was chaos when I woke up. Clipboards everywhere. But Sarah kept her head. You notice that, lying here.

monitoring_discussed: ^Mrs Kowalski: Last night we were all on that big screen. Then it went dark.
^Mrs Kowalski: Now it's a nurse with a clipboard every hour. If something happens between rounds...

c-0: ^Mrs Kowalski: I know they are. But there's a reason they invented that screen.
c-1: ^Mrs Kowalski: Not me. That poor man in Bed 4. His machine's been beeping since before I woke up.
c-2: ^Mrs Kowalski: I hope so. That screen was a comfort, you know. Somebody always watching.

pump_concern: ^Mrs Kowalski: That lady in Bed 2. Since her pump was changed she's gone very quiet, and her breathing's slow.
^Mrs Kowalski: Could you get someone? I don't like making a fuss, but I don't like that.

c-0: ^Mrs Kowalski: Thank you. Quickly, love. Shout for her, she'll hear you.
c-1: ^Mrs Kowalski: Maybe. I've been in hospital enough to know the difference.

drug_safety_concern: ^Mrs Kowalski: The pharmacist was round. He says they're doing the drips by hand until the computer's checked.
^Mrs Kowalski: Somebody's been at the computer that does the medicines? From outside? That's a lot to take in from a hospital bed.

c-0: ^Mrs Kowalski: I suppose a person can see what they're doing. A machine just does what it's told.
c-1: ^Mrs Kowalski: Good. I'd rather wait for a careful nurse than have a quick mistake.

hub: ^Have you noticed anything on the ward?
^How are you managing without the monitors?
^Has anyone told you about the medicines?
^Thank you for looking out for the ward.

c-0: ^Mrs Kowalski: That lady in Bed 2. Her drip's nearly empty, and that machine keeps bleeping and nobody's come.
^Mrs Kowalski: Somebody ought to see to her. Her pain will be back soon.
c-3: ^Mrs Kowalski: Somebody has to say when something doesn't feel right. Even from a bed.

state_sedated: ^Mrs Kowalski: I'm not sure she's all right. She was trying to call out, but she can't wake up properly. Is that normal?
state_critical: ^Mrs Kowalski: Please, someone look at her. She's not responding. I've been pressing the bell and nobody's coming!
state_deceased: ^Mrs Kowalski: She stopped breathing. I kept pressing the bell. I kept pressing it.
bed2_saved: ^Mrs Kowalski: They got to her. The nurse came running with something in a syringe, and she's breathing again.
